extracted.intended_audience: independent publishers, small-press editors, indie authors, and readers of the independent publishing industry
extracted.subtask_description: A feature/profile of an independent/small press (Cleis Press) describing its editorial standards, business practices, promotional strategies, and what the publisher looks for in books and authors. Useful for understanding selection and success criteria at a small press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary excellence / prose quality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is writing that 'sings off the page' that sets us apart; books must be 'really well-written.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate Publisher Brenda Knight says literary excellence is a requisite from the press's beginnings; Felice Newman’s background in poetry and writing has informed a standard of high-quality prose (e.g., 'literary erotica' that is 'really hot' and 'really well-written').

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling strength
rubrics_metrics.description: The key to a great book is great storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond craft and voice, a strong narrative that engages readers is explicitly emphasized as central to a book's success ('the key to a great book is great storytelling').

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality visual and interior design
rubrics_metrics.description: Unbending demand for only the best photographs and interior design to achieve a standard of excellence in the look and feel of books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frédérique Delacoste’s 'artistic eye' and insistence on top-tier photography and interior design are credited with nurturing the press's aesthetic standard; physical presentation is treated as part of editorial quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche/editorial focus
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear editorial niche—e.g., literary erotica and queer-focused titles—helps define the press's identity and catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleis’s history as a lesbian, feminist, and queer press and its emphasis on 'literary erotica' indicate a purposeful specialty that guides acquisitions and branding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful, sustainable growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not double production rapidly; add a few titles each year and avoid overextending resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Felice Newman: 'not doubling production from one year to the next' and 'we are growing, adding a few titles each year'—the publisher prioritizes steady, manageable growth rather than rapid expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial prudence / cash-flow-driven decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep growth and new projects in line with cash flow; avoid debt beyond essential obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press operates with no line of credit and 'no debt beyond our printing bills,' paying bills monthly; they will not pursue a project or campaign unless they can reasonably expect cash flow to cover it—this is an acquisition/production constraint as well as a policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective project acceptance based on funding viability
rubrics_metrics.description: Only undertake projects and promotional campaigns when funding/cash flow reasonably covers them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If they can't reasonably expect cash flow to cover a new project or campaign, 'we simply do not do it'—this is an explicit gating criterion for accepting work or launching initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author platform and publicity potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who tour extensively or have media visibility (columns, TV appearances, web presence) contribute to a title's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: authors who toured 40–75+ events, authors who write for major outlets or appeared on national TV (Oprah), and 'web-celeb' status are highlighted as assets that help sales and attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative marketing and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives and key relationships (imprints, book clubs, partnerships) are important facets of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleis cites launching the SexIs Bookclub with Eden Fantasies and the Viva Editions imprint as examples of innovative initiatives that drew attention and supported sales; strategic partnerships and new imprints are treated as growth and marketing levers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record / sales performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrable sales success and a track record of good-selling books support credibility and continued investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viva Editions' 'runaway bestseller' (Living Life as a Thank You, 30,000 books sold) and note that 2009 sales were up over 2008 are used as evidence of success—sales figures and track record matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenacity and long-term survival
rubrics_metrics.description: Longevity, persistence, and the ability to survive market downturns are valued attributes of a successful independent press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleis is described as a 'publishing survivor' celebrating 30 years and surviving when many contemporaries folded; this culture of tenacity is presented as integral to the press's identity and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curatorial/editorial rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders and editors maintain high editorial standards and a consistent demand for the best work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The founders' and editors' ongoing, hands-on insistence on quality (e.g., 'unbending demand for only the best' and the founders' influence since the start) functions as a selection and editing standard shaping the press's catalog.
